excerpt: WeLab is a Hong Kong fintech group behind WeLab Bank, one of the city's first virtual banks, with lending businesses in Hong Kong and Indonesia.
content:
WeLab is a Hong Kong financial technology group. It was founded in January 2013 by Simon Loong, Kelly Wong and Frances Kang, and Loong remains group chief executive. It began as an online consumer lender and is best known today as the parent of WeLab Bank, which received one of Hong Kong's first virtual banking licences in 2019 and operates as an app-only bank for retail customers.

The group also runs lending and banking businesses in Indonesia. Forbes reported that WeLab, together with Astra, bought a controlling stake in Bank Jasa Jakarta for $240 million, and that it operates the Maucash lending product there. WeLab became a unicorn after a 2017 funding round. Its backers over the years include Sequoia Capital, Allianz X, the International Finance Corporation and China Construction Bank, and Forbes put its total funding at about $900 million.

In 2019 WeLab raised a $156 million Series C, which FinTech Futures reported would fund the launch of WeLab Bank. In January 2026 the company announced a $220 million Series D, a mix of debt and equity, with investors including Prudential Hong Kong, Fubon Bank (Hong Kong), the Hong Kong Investment Corporation, TOM Group, Allianz X and HSBC. WeLab said it was the largest digital banking capital raise in Asia for 2025, and described WeLab Bank as the largest digital bank in Hong Kong by revenue. It did not disclose a valuation. The Asian Banker reported that WeLab Bank reached profitability in December 2024.

WeLab is not a software product you buy. For customers, WeLab Bank offers savings, deposits, loans and wealth products through its app, with fees set out in the bank's own tariff. It is relevant to readers following Asian digital banks and fintech.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
